**Visual observations from test image:**
- Close-up of a soybean stem at a node
- Green, healthy-looking stem with visible trichomes (hairs)
- **Gray/white fluffy mold growth concentrated at the node junction**
- Surrounding leaves are yellow and senescent (fallen/yellowed)
- The fluffy growth matches the mycelial character of White Mold

**Comparison with White_Mold reference:**
The reference collage clearly shows white/gray fluffy mycelial growth at stem nodes — exactly matching the test image. The gray fluffy mass at the node, combined with the green stem and senescent surrounding foliage, is characteristic of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum) at a node.

The key distinguishing feature — fluffy white/gray mycelium at the stem node — rules out other diseases like Diaporthe (black pycnidia in rows), Charcoal Rot (black microsclerotia), and Green_stem_disorder (no mycelial growth).
